question: What is the full form of PDF in the context of file formats?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Portable Document Format**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** full form **of the **term PDF **is **Portable Document Format**.
 
• It **stores text **and **images **and **can be opened **on **any Operating System (OS**), which, **in turn**, **makes it **easy **to share and store**.
 
• To **elaborate further**, the **PDF **was **created back **in the **early '90s **to **realize **the **dream of a sustainable**, **paperless office**.
 
• **Developed by Adobe**, a **PDf file **can** capture all **the **elements **of **a printed document **as an **electronic image**.
 
• **With PostScript**, every **individual PDF file **can retain the **text**, **formatting**, **vectors**, and even **fonts of the original document**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A computer **is a **digital electronic machine **that can be **programmed **to **carry out sequences **of **arithmetic **or **logical operations automatically**.
 
• **Modern computers **can **perform generic **sets of **operations known as programs**.
 
• **These programs **enable **computers to perform **a wide **range of tasks**.
